newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders say soybean sales to U.S. likely.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders say soybean sales to U.S. likely.

text.p: Brazilian traders said current prices were favoring sales of soybeans to the U.S. and reported talk that four cargoes had been sold in recent days.
"I heard that 7.2 million bushels have been done, that would amount to four cargoes," said one trader.
Brazilian soybeans are currently being offered at a discount of 30 cents per bushel to Chicago for July shipment, while for September shipment they are at a premium of 95 cents.
"In the U.S., it is just the other way around," said a soymeal trader, referring to the lower price of the November contract on Chicago Board of Trade compared to the July contract.
"With this spread between July and November, there is a lot of interest in people selling the product now and buying back later," said the soymeal trader.

Having committed a large percentage of its current harvest, Brazil was likely to follow in the footsteps of Argentina, which last week was said to have bought U.S. soybeans for November shipment, he added.

Buyers were chasing South American beans amid relief that there was still plenty of supply, following several weeks during which farmers held off selling as Chicago prices slid, said David Brew, trader at Brasoja.
"When Chicago started falling, farmers really held off selling," said Brew.
This was shortly after China was reputed to have bought between 500,000 and 700,000 tonnes soybeans and soymeal from the U.S., Brazil and Argentina, raising fears that supply would dry up.

"Suddenly, a lot of people are chasing the product now that China has been and gone," he said. "Chicago went back up and suddenly farmers are selling. People are relieved that supply is not running out."
However, traders agreed that it only made sense to buy Brazilian beans for July shipment and any sellers would have to have a vessel lined up and ready to go to make the trade worthwhile.
